page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; below the text, two notes in smaller type (under the text, marked (q) and (r)). Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: contra Morini praefationem quasi junćto umbone ediderunt Taylorus & Bootius, homines è secta Protestantium, quorum ille Anglus, hic verò Batavus; sed illorum omnium conviciis ac maledictis injuriarum plaustra reddit Morinus, {q}adeo[?] vili venerunt convicia ac maledicta apud istam Theologorum gentem furentem saepius ratione. Muisius iterum ad novam adversus Morinum scriptionem se accingit, quâ responsum illius castigat, & castigationis suae initium ducit ab explicatione sententiae libri proverbiorum, quae diversa plane ratione in hoc libro concipitur, nimirum, {r} Ne respondeas stulto juxta stultitiam ejus, ne sibi sapiens esse videatur; & quasi de illa explicanda ageretur, testes profert quosdam Judaeo-rum Magistros, sed revera tunc alludebat ad Morini nomen, sicut alias Erasmus homo facetissimus celeberrimi illiusMo-rini nomen intuebatur, cum Librum su-um
{q} Mor. in diatribe Elenctica & Animadv. in censur. edit. in 8. Parif. Anno 1639.
{r} Muif.[?] castig. anim. Parif.[?] in 8. Anno 1639.

page.notes: The first line "umbone" and the word "adeo" carry a smudge; "adeo" is read with [?]. In the notes, "Muif." and "Parif." are partly obscured by a stain. The printed run-ons "illiusMo-rini" and "adMorini" have no space in the print and are copied as printed. The mark on "ædeo" is a blot, not a letter. Catchword "um" is the start of the next page's word "um", so the word "Librum su-" continues there.
